newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek seamen end crippling 10-day stike.
newsitem.headline: Greek seamen end crippling 10-day stike.

text.p: Greek seamen on Thursday ended a crippling 10-day strike that left hundreds of trucks stranded at ports around the country and caused food and fuel shortages on islands.
A Panhellenic Seamen's Federation (PNO) official said the union decided to abandon the strike after all-night negotiations with the government.
The official said the government offered improved proposals on PNO demands for better benefits and measures against unemployment.
"There were all-night negotiations and the decision is to end the strike," the official told Reuters.

Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis, whose tough economic policies have prompted strong reaction from unions, called for an urgent meeting with the seamen late on Wednesday as soon as he returned from a European Socialists meeting in Rome.
The seamen's strike had paralysed sea transport, leaving thousands of tonnes of farm produce rotting at ports and cutting off remote Aegean islands that depend on ferries to survive in the winter.
